items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are clear (decodeClippedShape, maxDecodePrealloc, shapeIndexEncodingMagic). A header comment documents the wire layout, and the non-obvious parts are commented. Short names like s/e/d/p/l follow the package's own Go receiver and helper style.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Ignores the project conventions: it adds its own `shapeKind` enum instead of using typeTag, and puts every per-shape encoder in shapeindex_encode.go (499 lines) instead of next to each type. It also re-implements Polygon/Loop encoding. decodeShapeIndex is about 85 lines.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Validation is strong: lengths are bounded, IDs and edges are range-checked, there is a CRC, and a failed decode leaves the index unchanged. But Decode has a catch-all `recover()` that turns any panic into an error and can hide real bugs. Loop originInside, depth and bounds are trusted from the stream unvalidated.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: The change only adds methods. Existing Polygon/Polyline/Rect wire formats, typeTag values and the exported Shape interface are untouched. It defines its own private shapeKind instead of renumbering any tags.
